commit.message: Mac: add IQ3_S 256K performance to README
metal: specialize canonical resident expert down

bench: the 2026-10-03 Metal runs' raw output stays on the measuring machine

Finishes the trim the user chose on 2026-10-03 ("is bench/ supposed to be committed?" -> option 1). Each run's raw
output subdirectory (engine.log, results.json, config.json, monitor.jsonl, ...) is untracked: 352 files, 6.9 MB.
The 2026-10-04 folders already keep their run/ local.

Still in git:
- every directory's README, summaries, audit comparisons and drivers, and the top-level build/ctest/audit logs;
- the microbenchmarks (decode-opt2/micro, prefill-opt/micro), iq2-xs-opt/tiled and decode-opt/baseline/results.json;
- the frozen inputs the 10K MTP repro names: mtp-on/request.json, mtp-on/server-config.json and
  mtp-off/prompt-tokens.txt.

This is a plain commit, not a history rewrite. metal-mac is the default branch now, with three commits on top, so
f90370f still has every removed file (`git show f90370f:<path>`). The READMEs and .gitignore say so, and
.gitignore's older "run logs stay tracked" comment now says the top-level logs.

Mac: speeds re-measured in Energy Mode Automatic; Low Power and High Power compared

The earlier Mac numbers were taken in Low Power Mode. Same binary, configs and inputs, plugged in:

- Automatic (the README's numbers now): IQ2_XS 29 tok/s writing, 277 reading 30K, 203 reading
  128K; Q2_0 27 / 276 / 204. Low Power was 15-16% slower writing and 26-30% slower reading.
- High Power measured no faster than Automatic (-4.4% to +1.3%, two High Power runs differ by 3.4%).
- Output is word for word the same in all three modes. Picture encodings are byte for byte the
  same. GPU memory is identical across modes.
- MTP drafts stay off: --mtp-max-t 2 is 23-27% slower in both Automatic and High Power.
- long_context.py pins its 128K corpus to commit dc047b5 (--corpus-rev) and records the prompt hash.
  The earlier Low Power 128K prompt differed because the docs had been edited between runs.
- Each bench folder keeps *.json (Automatic) beside *.low-power.json and *.high-power.json.

Mac: pictures on the GPU, Q2_0 and 128K measured, an arrow-key model list every run, Mac-only README

Pictures: setup builds strata-vision (llama.cpp mtmd) with ggml's Metal backend, downloads the mmproj and
turns images on by default (--vision no turns them off). The Metal encoder matches the CPU one (median row
cosine 0.99998; 2 of 2,178 rows under 0.9) at 0.4-1.4 s a picture against 1-4.5 min on the CPU. Through the
server all 7 checks pass (receipt text, shapes and colours, counting, Chinese text, a screenshot, a
follow-up, text only), and with --vision the five README runs give the same text at the same speed.

Q2_0 (native pack): 22.5-22.8 tok/s writing, 205 reading. 128K context: IQ2_XS 141 / Q2_0 143 tok/s
reading, 24.5 / 23.1 writing, the planted fields 3/3, a follow-up reusing 128,025 tokens answers in 0.9 s.

setup on a Mac shows the supported models (data/mac-metal.json's menu) every run, picked with the arrow
keys; downloaded ones first; in brackets the download state, the fit to this Mac's memory (recommended,
fits, tight, too little) and the measured speed. Under 20 GB it stops. --yes or no terminal takes the
model used last or the recommended one. A model file of 1 GB or more comes over four connections
(resumable plan), every file is checked against the SHA-256 Hugging Face publishes, the original's
shared shard 2 is linked instead of downloaded, and a setup again keeps hand-edited config keys.

README: Mac only (the PC install, Windows scripts and PC model table are gone); the speed, 128K and
model tables are this Mac's measurements. tools/test_setup_mac.py: 48 tests; every setup test and the
146 serve tests pass, test_setup_golden unchanged.

Mac one-click install: setup.sh builds the Metal engine, download-model.sh, model files in Strata-data/

On an Apple-Silicon Mac, ./setup.sh now installs and starts the measured Metal version instead of stopping:
it checks the Mac (Apple Silicon, memory, Xcode's Metal compiler; a missing Metal Toolchain is downloaded
after asking), compiles the engine into engine/strata, prepares IQ2_XS and writes strata-iq2_xs.json with
the settings of data/mac-metal.json (32K, every expert resident, MTP off). Later runs start it; a git pull
that changes the engine's source recompiles it.

./download-model.sh (setup --download-only) fetches the model files alone, resumable and never twice;
--data-dir and --gguf-dir choose where, and setup remembers them. The model files live in the git-ignored
Strata-data/ inside the folder, and the config names everything by paths relative to it (the server, setup
and the MCP status resolve relative paths against the config's folder). HF_ENDPOINT picks a mirror.

CMakeLists.txt: the Metal engine target sat inside the tests' block, so STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF built no
strata; it is outside now (with tests on, the same 50 tests).

Measured on the M2 Max: setup compiles the engine in 25 s, and its install writes 23.8-23.9 tok/s and reads
a 30,000-token prompt at 198 tok/s with the same output text as the measured build
(bench/results/2026-10-03-metal-setup/). tools/test_setup_mac.py: 33 tests; every setup test and the 146
serve tests pass, test_setup_golden unchanged (the PC path is the same).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Metal backend for Apple Silicon: the engine on a Mac, exact decode and prefill kernels

Ports the CUDA/HIP engine to Metal (-DSTRATA_ENABLE_METAL=ON, docs/PORT_METAL/):
a CUDA-runtime shim over Metal (buffers, streams, events, graphs as replayed tapes),
every src/kernels/cuda file as MSL + launcher behind the same headers, the prefill
GEMMs, and the engine/server link. Runs IQ2_XS on an M2Max (96 GB) end to end.

Decode (rounds 22-23, 26): threadgroup-codebook IQ4_XS/NL, direct Q2_0 / IQ3_S dots,
one-pass hyper-connection norm, GDN last-token write-back and no second GDN
recurrence in the commit, parallel QSA top-k. Warm decode on the frozen 10K
prompt 18.8 -> 22.6 tok/s, 2.24 GiB less memory (no IQ4 view).

Prefill (round 25): 64x64 FP16/BF16 GEMM tiles, register prompt attention, wider
expert tiles. 10K prompt 123 -> 194 tok/s.

Every change keeps each output's arithmetic: metal_direct_dot_test compares the new
kernels to the originals bit for bit (51M outputs); the real-model audit matches
96,596,480 logits and 6 committed states bitwise. Each change has a =0 switch.
CTest 50/50. Evidence, scripts and microbenchmarks: bench/results/2026-10-03-metal*.
docs/MAC.md documents the Mac setup, including the experimental Metal backend.
